assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pore architecture and active-site placement (organic structure-directing agents, new framework topologies, tailored acidity and metal sites) underpins refining, petrochemistry and emissions control at enormous scale. It is a clear case of structure determining function, and solving these frameworks depended on crystallographic methods that I know well from my own work.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalytic design and industrial transfer), Zones (structure-directing agents, SSZ materials, Chevron practice) and Davis (new framework discovery, hierarchical and Lewis-acid zeolites) are the strongest trio. Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis are important but later or more specialised contributors. Credit is broad across a large community, so any three-name configuration omits significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and industrial deployment; the field is mature and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: The discovery is a diffuse field rather than one sharply defined event, making a three-person cut contentious.
Zeolite science itself has long-standing earlier pioneers outside the credited list, who are not on this list and cannot be proposed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in little more than a decade, a remarkable materials-chemistry story with a defined structure-property basis and global impact on photovoltaics research.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park the solid-state cell with long-lived high efficiency, and Snaith the thin-film and meso-superstructured perovskite devices that showed the material works as a true absorber. Kanatzidis and Grätzel also have strong claims; the three-person limit forces a contested choice.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency records are repeatedly confirmed across many laboratories. Long-term operational stability, lead toxicity and commercial scale-up are not settled, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Device durability and manufacturability remain open.
Priority and credit are disputed among several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Supported single-atom catalysts maximise metal utilisation and give well-defined active sites that link molecular and heterogeneous catalysis. The concept has reshaped catalyst design and drew strongly on atomic-resolution electron microscopy and X-ray absorption for evidence.
assessment.attribution: The 2011 Pt1/FeOx work from Zhang, Qiao and colleagues, with Jingyue Liu's earlier and parallel contributions on isolated atoms, is the core. Credit to Abhaya Datye, Jun Li and Aiqin Wang is substantial and the allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced but the field is still young. Debate continues over true site uniformity, stability under reaction conditions and distinguishing single atoms from small clusters, so it may be premature.
uncertainties: Structural proof of isolated sites under operating conditions is often indirect or based on averaged or limited-area data.
Priority is shared among several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The atomic structure of the nitrogenase MoFe protein, with the FeMo-cofactor and its interstitial carbide, explains how biology reduces dinitrogen. This is a landmark result in bioinorganic structural chemistry, resting on high-quality crystallographic evidence that I can judge directly.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle provided the decisive crystal structures (the cofactor, the central carbide, high resolution). Dean's genetics and biochemistry set the foundation. Seefeldt and Ribbe contributed mechanistic and biosynthetic work, so allocation is not trivial.
assessment.maturity: The structure is firmly established and independently confirmed. The catalytic mechanism is still debated, so the prize would have to rest on structure rather than a settled mechanism.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 binding and reduction remains incompletely resolved.
Whether the discovery should be cast as structure or mechanism affects who is credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from micro- and nanocrystals and time-resolved studies of reactions, an enabling method that opened structural chemistry to samples and timescales previously out of reach. It is closely related to my own interest in small-crystal structure determination.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the demonstration and method development, Fromme the membrane-protein crystals and sample strategies, Schlichting the time-resolved applications and instrumentation. I am uncertain about Janos Hajdu's current status and the proper weight of his early role.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by multiple facilities, but the facilities are few and the chemical impact is still growing, so recognition is slightly early compared with cryo-EM and synchrotron methods. Competing small-crystal methods such as 3D electron diffraction and microED address overlapping needs.
uncertainties: Relative influence of the individuals within a large collaboration is unclear.
Limited access to XFEL facilities may limit breadth of impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imaging the internal bond structure of single molecules with a CO-functionalised tip made molecular structure directly visible and enables determination of unknown on-surface structures and reaction products, with a very clear and original central result.
assessment.attribution: Gross and Meyer (IBM Zurich) produced the 2009 CO-tip bond imaging; Giessibl's qPlus sensor was the technical basis. Eigler and Ho have separate claims in single-atom and single-molecule manipulation and spectroscopy that lie partly outside this discovery.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely, but the scope is limited to well-defined surface-bound molecules, so general chemical impact is narrower than for bulk structural methods.
uncertainties: Attribution between imaging and manipulation lines of work is not clean.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is one of the most used reactions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, with very high practical and lasting impact. Its originality is somewhat reduced by the earlier recognition of Pd cross-coupling in 2010.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general, ligand-enabled amination methods; Kosugi's tin-amide precedent is earlier but narrower. A two-person award is clear.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and industrially embedded for decades; timing is not premature.
uncertainties: The committee may view it as incremental to the 2010 coupling prize.
Kosugi's precedent could be argued as part of the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal tRNA-synthetase pairs lets cells incorporate designed non-canonical amino acids into proteins, a powerful tool for chemistry within living systems.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the orthogonal pair approach and the first cases in bacteria and yeast; Chin extended it to multicellular organisms, multiple codons and engineered ribosomes. Lei Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama also made important contributions.
assessment.maturity: The technology is widely used and independently validated, though practical impact is mostly in research tools rather than established applications; timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Allocation among several early contributors is open.
Therapeutic and industrial impact remains emerging.
